name: spfront
what_it_does: Feeds the speedometer and odometer math. Set this to the actual tooth count of the front sprocket you have installed. The FX/FXS factory sprocket is 20 teeth. This value affects only the displayed speed, trip distance, and Wh-per-km — it changes no physical parameter.
caution: Benign to get wrong (display math only), but a wrong value will make the speedo, odometer, and energy-efficiency numbers wrong. After a re-gear, set this before relying on any distance or speed readings.

name: sprear
what_it_does: Feeds the speedometer and odometer math. Set this to the actual tooth count of the rear sprocket installed. The FX/FXS factory rear sprocket is 90 teeth. Display math only — no physical effect on the drivetrain.
caution: Display math only; no physical effect. Wrong value skews speed and odo readings. For a 56-tooth rear sprocket, enter 56.

name: rwhcirc
what_it_does: Sets the rear wheel circumference used in speedometer calculations. Trim this value until your speedo matches a GPS fix. Typical range is 1900–2000 mm depending on tire size and inflation. Display math only.
caution: Display math only. Too high = speedo reads slower than actual; too low = reads faster. Verify against a GPS, not a stopwatch estimate.

name: maxcustspmph
what_it_does: Sets the top speed cap when riding in Custom ride mode. The bike's physical ceiling is around 85 mph; the console accepts values up to 102. This is a factory-supported parameter — the bike has always been designed to accept it.
caution: Factory-supported and safe within the 20–102 mph range. Setting it above the bike's actual top speed is harmless (the drivetrain limit still applies). Setting it very low restricts Custom mode to a slow crawl.

name: maxcusttq_allowed
plain_name: Custom mode: max torque (% of allowed)
what_it_does: Caps available torque in Custom mode, expressed as a percentage of the maximum the Sevcon motor controller permits. 100% = full torque available to Custom mode; 10% = very mild acceleration.
caution: Factory-supported. Lower values reduce acceleration authority in Custom mode only. Eco and Sport modes are unaffected.

name: maxcustregcotq_allow
plain_name: Custom mode: coast regen (% of allowed)
what_it_does: Sets the regenerative braking strength when you roll off the throttle (coast) in Custom mode, as a percentage of what the Sevcon allows. Lower values give a more free-coasting feel and improve efficiency. Higher values give stronger engine-braking.
caution: Exactly 0% is refused by the app — zero coast regen can cause the rear wheel to momentarily unload on slippery surfaces (fishtail risk). Use a small nonzero value such as 5% for a near-freewheel feel.

name: maxcustregbrtq_allow
plain_name: Custom mode: brake regen (% of allowed)
what_it_does: Sets the regen braking force applied when the brake switch closes (i.e. when you pull the brake lever) in Custom mode, as a percentage of what the Sevcon allows. 0% disables brake-lever-triggered regen in Custom mode; 100% applies maximum allowed brake regen.
caution: Factory-supported. At 0% the brake lever triggers no regen in Custom mode. High values add significant electrical braking on top of hydraulic brakes — test in a safe area before riding normally.

name: brakeregen
what_it_does: Master switch that determines whether the brake light switch triggers regenerative braking at all. When set to Yes (the default), pulling either brake lever applies max brake regen in addition to hydraulic braking. When set to No, brake-lever regen is disabled globally.
caution: Affects brake feel in every ride mode. Make only modest changes and test in a parking lot. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike — it may not appear in your set dump even after login.

name: brakefilter
what_it_does: Millisecond delay after the brake switch closes before the brake light and regen activate. The default is approximately 100 ms. Increasing it debounces a noisy brake switch; decreasing it makes brake light and regen response more immediate.
caution: Keep this near the default (100 ms). Too high = perceptible brake-light lag. Too low = possible switch chatter causing spurious regen pulses. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.

name: noregenstopped
what_it_does: When Yes (the default), blocks regenerative braking below roughly 13 mph, which prevents the rear wheel from locking up or skidding during very slow manoeuvring. When set to No, regen can activate at any speed including walking pace.
caution: This is a low-speed stability guard. Disabling it (No) removes that guard. The app will warn you if you try to set it to No. Leave it Yes unless you have a specific, well-understood reason. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.

name: reserve_sw
what_it_does: Enables or disables the battery reserve partition feature. When Yes, the bike withholds a configurable percentage of state-of-charge as a 'reserve' that the gauge treats like an empty tank before tapping into it. The actual pack capacity is unchanged — this is purely a gauge and range-planning feature.
caution: Gauge behavior only — adds zero real amp-hours. On an aged pack, disabling the reserve (No) or shrinking it removes a low-SoC safety margin that helps avoid deep discharge. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.

name: reserve_pct
what_it_does: The percentage of battery SoC the reserve partition withholds before the gauge shows empty. Default is 33%. Raising it makes the gauge hit 'empty' earlier in real terms; lowering it lets you run the pack further before the gauge reads zero.
caution: Gauge behavior only. Reducing below the default gives less visual warning before the pack approaches its true lower limit — this matters more on an aged, reduced-capacity pack. Accepts 0–50%. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.

name: fuelgaugepes
what_it_does: A display buffer that shifts the shown SoC percentage downward by this many points so the gauge reads a bit lower than the calculated state-of-charge. Default is 5%. At 5%, a calculated 20% SoC displays as 15%. This only shifts the number shown — it does not change how the pack charges or discharges.
caution: Reducing below 5% removes a displayed-SoC safety buffer that helps avoid unexpectedly deep discharge, especially on an aged pack where SoC calculations drift. The app warns if you set it below 5%. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.

name: chgstby
what_it_does: How long (in minutes) the BMS sleeps after reaching 100% charge before waking to run a cell balancing pass. The default is 1440 minutes (24 hours). A shorter interval means the BMS balances cells more frequently after a full charge; a longer interval reduces how often it wakes.
caution: Affects cell balancing cadence. The 24-hour default is appropriate for typical daily use. Setting it very short (e.g. 60 minutes) causes the BMS to wake and balance frequently, which is generally harmless but unnecessary. Setting it very long (e.g. 10080 = 7 days) delays balancing on a pack with drifting cells. NOT confirmed present on the verified 2017 FXS rev-41 bike.
